L0@P0: THE POP-STACK OPERATOR ON ORNAMENTATION LATTICES
L1@P0: KHALID AJRAN AND COLIN DEFANT
L2@P0: Abstract. Each rooted plane tree T has an associated ornamentation lattice O(T). The ornamentation lattice of an n-element chain is the n-th Tamari lattice. We study the pop-stack operator
L3@P0: Pop: O(T) → O(T), which sends each element δ to the meet of the elements covered by or equal
L4@P0: to δ. We compute the maximum size of a forward orbit of Pop on O(T), generalizing a result of
L5@P0: Defant for Tamari lattices. We also characterize the image of Pop on O(T), generalizing a result of
L6@P0: Hong for Tamari lattices. For each integer k ≥ 0, we provide necessary conditions for an element
L7@P0: of O(T) to be in the image of Popk. This allows us to completely characterize the image of Popk
L8@P0: on a Tamari lattice.
L9@P0: 1. Introduction
L10@P0: 1.1. Ornamentation Lattices. Laplante-Anfossi [15] recently introduced remarkable polytopes
L11@P0: called operahedra. These polytopes are special examples of graph associahedra [5, 17] and poset
L12@P0: associahedra [13], and they generalize both the associahedra and permutohedra. Laplante-Anfossi
L13@P0: also considered certain posets obtained by orienting the 1-skeletons of operahedra, and he asked
L14@P0: if these posets are lattices. Defant and Sack [11] answered Laplante-Anfossi’s question in the
L15@P0: affirmative, naming his posets operahedron lattices. A key idea that Defant and Sack employed was
L16@P0: to embed an operahedron lattice into the product of an interval in the weak order on the symmetric
L17@P0: group and another lattice. This other lattice, which is the primary focus of this article, is a new
L18@P0: structure called an ornamentation lattice.

L55@P1: 1.2. Pop-Stack Operators. The pop-stack operator of a finite lattice L is the map Pop: L → L
L56@P1: defined by
L57@P1: Pop(x) = ^({x} ∪ {y ∈ L : y ⋖ x}).
L58@P1: Initial works on this operator focused on the case where L is the weak order on the symmetric group
L59@P1: [1,2,7,8,16,18,20], where it can be interpreted as a deterministic sorting procedure that makes use
L60@P1: of a data structure called a pop-stack. Several recent articles have studied pop-stack operators on
L61@P1: other interesting lattices, especially from a dynamical point of view [4,6,9,10,12,14]. For example,
L62@P1: Defant [10] and Hong [14] found that the pop-stack operator on a Tamari lattice has particularly
L63@P1: well behaved dynamics. Choi and Sun [6] and Barnard, Defant, and Hanson [4] later generalized
L64@P1: these results to the much broader class of Cambrian lattices. In this article, we generalize the results
L65@P1: about Tamari lattices in a different direction by considering pop-stack operators of ornamentation
L66@P1: lattices.
L67@P1: Given a finite lattice L and an element x ∈ L, we let OrbPop(x) = {x, Pop(x), Pop2(x), . . .} denote
L68@P1: the forward orbit of x under Pop. If t is a sufficiently large integer, then Popt(x) is the minimum

L75@P2: lattice of a finite Coxeter group W, then maxx∈L |OrbPop(x)| is equal to the Coxeter number of W.
L76@P2: In particular, if L is the n-th Tamari lattice (which is a Cambrian lattice of the symmetric group

L78@P2: Another important aspect of the pop-stack operator is its image, which has been studied for a
L79@P2: variety of lattices in [4,6,12,14,19]. Defant and Williams found numerous different interpretations
L80@P2: of the size of the image of Pop when L is a semidistributive lattice (or, more generally, a semidistrim
L81@P2: lattice). Notably, when L is semidistributive, the image of Pop is in bijection with the facets of
L82@P2: a simplicial complex called the canonical join complex of L (see [3, 4]). Hong [14] characterized

L84@P2: results for a variety of other lattices. Barnard, Defant, and Hanson then unified several of these
L85@P2: results by providing a simple Coxeter-theoretic description of the image of Pop on an arbitrary
L86@P2: Cambrian lattice of a finite Coxeter group. We aim to generalize Hong’s results concerning Tamari
L87@P2: lattices in a different direction by studying Pop images on ornamentation lattices.
